text: f) Reforms to the foreign exchange regime in Ethiopia
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) on 29 July 2024 announced a reform of the foreign exchange regime with immediate effect. The Foreign Exchange Directive No. FXD/01/2024 introduced major policy changes, allowing forex rates to be determined through negotiations between banks and customers. This marked a significant shift from prior practices and aimed to consolidate fragmented forex regulations and liberalize the financial sector.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The policy changes addressed the 13 elements below;
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: • Shift to a market-based exchange regime
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: • End of surrender requirements to the NBE
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: • Removal of import restrictions
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: • Improvement of retention rules for exporters
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: • Removal of rules governing banks’ allocation of foreign exchange
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: • Introduction of non-bank foreign exchange bureaus
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: • Removal of restrictions on franco-valuta imports
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: • Simplification of rules governing foreign currency accounts
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: • Allowance for residents to open foreign currency accounts
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: • Removal of interest rate ceilings
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: • Opening of Ethiopia’s securities market to foreign investors
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: • Granting of special foreign exchange privileges to companies within special economic zones
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: • Relaxation of various rules on the amount of foreign currency cash notes travellers may carry when travelling in and out of Ethiopia
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The following are the envisaged benefits of the FX regime reforms, amongst others;

text: i. Description of M-PESA Profile
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Description Item Transfers (P2P) This represents customer deposits in the M-PESA e-wallet that can be funded by direct cash deposits at agent level or through person to person (P2P) transfers. M-PESA Agents M-PESA Agents include Safaricom authorized dealers, operating one or more outlets around Kenya, retailers with a substantial distribution network like petrol stations, distributors, supermarkets, registered SMEs and selected Banks and Micro-Finance Institutions. Their key tasks include; registering M-PESA customers, depositing cash into registered customers’ M-PESA wallets, processing cash withdrawals for registered and non-registered M-PESA customers and compliance with Safaricom AML & KYC Policy and business practices. Withdrawals/ Withdrawal is the removal of e-money from M-PESA e-wallet to cash through M-PESA agents. Cash out Deposits/ Customers fund their M-PESA e-wallet through M-PESA agents or directly from their bank accounts. Cash in Payments C2B, B2C and Customer to Business (C2B) or Business to Customer (B2C) are mainly bank transfers while Business to Business (B2B) is for business transactions. These together with LNM transactions form the payments B2B channels in the M-PESA ecosystem. Lipa Na M-PESA LNM is a platform that enables merchants to transact using a till number to collect payments from customers. LNM has two major use cases; (LNM) • Buy Goods - mainly used for one-off payments to merchants, this is done ‘on the go’, mainly face to face but can also be done remotely. • Billers - This is the paybill option/C2B of LNM which mostly happens remotely/online and is mainly used for repetitive transactions done on utility payments to government agencies, SACCOs, electricity & water providers and hospitals. Pochi la Pochi La Biashara, translated to ‘Business Wallet’ in English, is a product that allows M-PESA registered customers who own informal businesses such as; food vendors, kiosk owners, boda-boda operators, Biashara second hand clothes dealers, etc. to receive and separate business funds from personal funds on their M-PESA line. Savings and Lending M-Shwari M-Shwari is a micro-lending/savings product in partnership with NCBA (a tier 1 Kenyan Bank). The M-Shwari Loan Account is a micro-credit product which allows customers to borrow money or to complement their savings towards an investment or enterprise.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY25
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Fuliza In partnership with Kenyan lenders, NCBA and KCB Bank, the Group operates an Overdraft (OD) facility dubbed ‘Fuliza’, a product that enables customers to access unsecured line of credit by overdrawing on M-PESA to cover short-term cash-flow shortfalls subject to an applicable pre-determined limit. Fuliza is available to all M-PESA customers, however the awarding of limits will depend on the customer’s credit scoring and how long they have been using M-PESA. Customers who ‘opt in’ on Fuliza are charged a one-off access fee and daily maintenance fees on unpaid loan amounts based on a pre-determined matrix. In partnership with ABSA Kenya, Timiza is a wallet solution that offers easy banking and instant loans to Timiza customers. Through *848# or the Timiza app customers are able to get an instant loan, save, send money, pay bills, purchase airtime, and get insurance with Timiza. Overdraft Merchant OD is a loan product offered by Safaricom in partnership with KCB Bank Kenya (KCB). The service enables business owners on Lipa Na M-PESA to complete payments even with insufficient funds in their till. facility for The service applies when making transactions from a Lipa Na M-PESA Business Till to other Till Numbers and businesses PayBill Numbers, when sending money to an individual, and when withdrawing to the nominated number (Merchant OD) or at an Agent. The service advances an overdraft of up to KShs 400,000 depending on the business’ limit. The overdraft is offered a 2% one off fee and a tiered daily access fee after the 24-hour free period. M-Kopa M-KOPA provides solar home systems that innovatively integrate machine-to-machine technology (M2M) with a micro-payment solution. The system includes embedded GSM technology for monitoring and metering usage, while its pay-as-you-go service carries the advantage of no large initial cash outlay. After an initial deposit, customers pay daily instalments via a mobile money service (M-PESA) until paying off the balance. Once this repayment is complete, customers own the unit outright. Importantly, this solution is cheaper and healthier than the alternative, kerosene lamps for rural households with no electricity. M-KOPA solar is currently available in 750 outlets nationwide in Kenya through the Safaricom distribution network. IMT M-PESA Global International Safaricom Plc through its fully owned subsidiary, Safaricom Money Transfer Services Limited (SMTSL), Money Transfer operates remittance services that allows customers to send and receive money to a beneficiary through (IMT) registered mobile phone numbers in partnership with third party International Money Remittance (IMT) providers. Revenue is earned from transaction fees charged to customers for international money transfers (inbound and outbound).

title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26

text: Financial Year 26 was a landmark year for Safaricom. Beyond delivering strong commercial performance, the year carried deep symbolic and strategic significance, marking 25 years of how our network, platforms, products and services have transformed lives and continue to improve everyday life for millions of Kenyans.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Through nationwide celebrations, grassroots engagements and community initiatives, we connected directly with Kenyans from all walks of life. These engagements directly shaped improvements in network experience, customer care, platform innovation and affordability, ensuring that the value we create is felt widely across our ecosystem.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: We remain deeply grateful to our customers, partners and communities who co created impact with us, not just by using our services, but by helping us reaffirmed our purpose of Transforming Lives and strengthened our responsibility services partner.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Purpose Driven Foundation Initiatives & ESG
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Through the Safaricom and M-PESA Foundations, we advanced digital inclusion, financial empowerment and youth opportunity, underpinned by a strong sustainability agenda. The launch of Citizens of the Future, our flagship education programme, expanded access to quality learning, digital tools and safe learning environments, creating long term opportunity for learners, teachers and communities nationwide. In health, maternal and childcare improved through Uzazi Salama, while free medical camps and telemedicine expanded access to quality care. Economic empowerment advanced through Wezesha Agri and Wezesha Mama, supporting youth and women with skills training, grants and digital tools. These initiatives reflect our inclusive approach to innovation, anchored in partnerships, purpose led brand storytelling and measurable national impact, while reinforcing Safaricom’s role as a catalyst for sustainable social and economic progress.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Operating Environment
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Safaricom continues to operate in a highly regulated environment, with evolving oversight across telecommunications, financial services, data protection, and digital platforms. FY26 benefitted from a stable and more predictable macroeconomic environment that enabled consistent execution and forward planning. In Kenya, inflation remained below 5% and GDP growth averaged around 5%. The Kenyan shilling held stable for most of the year, supporting business confidence and consumer spending. For customers, this translated into continued access to affordable connectivity and financial services during a period of high living costs.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: e e e Safaricom Ethiopia
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Our purpose in Ethiopia remains to transform lives for a digital future and our vision is to establish an innovative brand loved by our customers. We are building a world-class network focused on earning customer loyalty and are experimenting/learning from the
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: lessons and the challenges as the business evolves, to create a digital future for our customers guided by strong values in customer obsession, trust and respect, speed and innovation and compliance & integrity. Our brand has been established as a data network and our customers appreciate the superior customer experience we offer, reliable connectivity & speeds, as well as secure access to the fastest data network in Ethiopia.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: In Ethiopia, the operating environment remained stable, with GDP expanding 9.2% (2024/25) and inflation easing into single digits, driven by declining food inflation. This marked the lowest inflation levels since 2018 and reinforced the National Bank of Ethiopia’s achievement of its single digit inflation objective. ETB continued to depreciate against both the dollar and the Euro, with the second half of the year remaining stable compared to the first half. Industry-led regulations to build a sustainable industry on Reference Infrastructure Sharing Offer (RISO) and guidelines on cost of service for voice and mobile data, provided improved pricing clarity and predictability in operating conditions. The combination of macro stability, ongoing regulatory driven policy changes, and disciplined internal execution enabled the business to maintain momentum across our key segments.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Customer growth remained strong, underpinned by rising usage and increasing customer density, while network investment focused on optimising capacity and sweating existing assets in priority regions rather than aggressive footprint expansion. The business implemented price adjustments in December 2025 across key products, with further gradual adjustments expected as part of the phased implementation of the regulator mandated cost of service for voice and data. These pricing actions are supporting revenue repair while maintaining affordability in a market that continues to have among the lowest telecom prices in Africa, despite sustained inflationary pressures.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Key Business Updates
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: We successfully returned to the domestic bond market for the first time in over a decade, securing capital at competitive rates. The strong investor appetite reflected confidence in Safaricom’s fundamentals, balance sheet strength, and long-term strategy. Together with our Sustainability Linked Loan, this funding further aligns our capital structure with our sustainability commitments, linking financing terms to measurable progress in carbon reduction, digital inclusion, and social impact.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Across FY26, we maintained sharp focus on delivering scalable technology platforms that meet the evolving needs of our customers. In Kenya, continued expansion of 4G+ adoption supported broadband usage and digital content growth. In Ethiopia, we sustained rollout in priority towns and strengthened distribution to enhance availability and customer experience. The successful rollout of Fintech 2.0 enhanced stability, capacity and fraud controls, materially improving resilience while unlocking new customer and merchant experiences. This upgrade lays the foundation for platform monetisation and advanced capabilities, including Al driven reconciliation and ecosystem services. The launch of Ziidi Trader marked an important milestone, broadening access to capital markets and demonstrating early traction as a new driver of financial deepening and inclusion. We implemented data minimization to person-to-person transactions, with recipients only seeing two names and a masked number. This reflects our ongoing commitment to embedding privacy across our financial ecosystem.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: FY26 marked meaningful progress in advancing our Vision 2030- To become Africa’s leading purpose-led technology company, reaffirming our commitment to transforming lives and becoming a technology company that delivers inclusive digital and financial solutions across our markets. This progress was underpinned by the continued strength of our Kenya business and the steady scale up of Safaricom Ethiopia, despite a more complex operating environment.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Our ambition remains centred on delivering personalised, value adding services to our customers, while partnering with the public sector and stakeholders to accelerate digitisation. Connectivity and mobile financial services continue to form the backbone of this transformation. Through disciplined execution and sustained investment, we are strengthening the foundations for long term growth, expanding digital inclusion, and unlocking new opportunities for individuals, businesses, and communities across the Group.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: During the year, an interim dividend of KShs 0.85 per ordinary share (2025: KShs 0.55) amounting to KShs 34.06Bn (2025: KShs 22.04Bn) was declared and paid. The directors have proposed a final dividend in respect of the year ended 31 March 2026 of KShs 115 per ordinary share (2025: KShs 0.65) amounting to a total of KShs 46.08Bn (2025: KShs 26.04Bn) to be approved at the Annual general meeting (AGM) to be held on 31 July 2026. This brings the total dividend for the year to KShs 80.13Bn (2025: KShs 48.08Bn) which represents KShs 2.00 per share in respect of the year ended 31 March 2026 (2025: KShs 1.20 per share). The final dividend wil be payable on or about 4 September 2026 to the shareholders on the Register of Members as at the close of business on 4 August 2026.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Safaricom delivered a resilient performance in FY26 against a backdrop of continued macroeconomic pressure and heightened geopolitical disruption affecting supply chains and energy costs. Despite these headwinds, the Group sustained strong commercial momentum across both Kenya and Ethiopia, reflecting disciplined execution and reinforcing confidence in our strategic direction. FY26 marked the first full year of execution under Vision 2030, our ambition to become Africa’s leading purpose-led technology company. This strategy is anchored in customer-centric innovation, leveraging technology to deliver relevant, impactful solutions that deepen engagement, drive inclusion and create long-term value.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: In Kenya, we maintained robust performance across our core businesses, supported by strong customer activity, continued innovation and resilient execution. We focused on protecting affordability while competing on value and experience, enabling us to defend market leadership and deliver high-quality earnings. Our Enterprise and Digital businesses continued to scale, reflecting rising demand for connectivity, cloud, fintech and integrated digital solutions. In Ethiopia, we progressed from market entry to early scale. The successful launch of M-PESA, expanding network coverage and improving regulatory clarity represent important milestones as the market normalises. We remain focused on disciplined investment and commercial scaling as Ethiopia transitions toward becoming a sustainable second growth engine for the Group. Collectively, these outcomes underscore our commitment to protecting shareholder value, strengthening business resilience and positioning the Group for sustainable long-term growth.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: In FY27 we expect Group EBIT of KShs 180-187 billion and Group Capex of KShs 64—70 billion. Kenya EBIT is expected to be KShs 195-199 billion, with Ethiopia delivering an EBIT loss of KShs 12-15 billion as we continue to reduce startup losses. Kenya Capex is expected to be KShs 58-61 billion, with KShs 6—9 billion in Ethiopia. FY27 guidance numbers exclude IAS 29 impact. We remain confident in our ability to deliver on our strategic priorities, navigate near-term volatility and continue building a resilient, future-ready organisation well positioned to capture long-term opportunities.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: In FY27, we will accelerate growth by deepening customer value through more personalised, affordable, and integrated propositions, while scaling M PESA’s next frontier across merchant solutions, credit, savings, insurance, wealth, and cross border payments. We will also advance Al driven customer experience, network optimisation, and productivity across the business, strengthening our digital capabilities. At the same time, we will grow Safaricom Ethiopia sustainably as mobile financial services unlock new revenue pools, while reinforcing our sustainability, climate, and digital inclusion commitments.

text: Business Review — Group
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: We are pleased to report a strong performance for FY26, reflecting the Group’s resilience and strategic focus amidst a dynamic operating environment. Group Service Revenue grew by 11.5% YoY to KShs 414.1Bn, driven by double digit growth in Kenya and accelerated growth in Ethiopia. Profitability improved in line with revenue growth, supported by disciplined cost management and operational efficiencies, enabling strong cash generation to support ongoing investment and shareholder returns. Our customer base also expanded significantly, with total Group three-month active customers rising by 25.4% to 71.56Mn, and one month active customers increasing by 14.2% to 50.66Mn.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: In Kenya, the macroeconomic environment remained stable and supportive, with inflation contained below 5%, while GDP grew by 4.6% (2025), and the Kenyan shilling broadly stable at approximately 129/USD. This stability continued to support customer usage, affordability and overall investor confidence. Against this backdrop, Safaricom Kenya sustained its market leadership, maintaining a 66.8% GSM customer market share as at December 2025, according to the Communications Authority of Kenya.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: In Ethiopia, inflation eased to single digit, 9.4% as at March 2026. However, the Birr depreciated by 23.7% against the US Dollar in FY26 to 154.96 as at 31 March 2026 while it weakened by 39.6% to 180.96 against the Euro in the same period. This FX impact has been reflected in our consolidated financial statements. Ethiopia is moving into a more stable, scaling business phase, clearer regulation (cost of service pricing, Reference Interconnection Offer (RIO)/ Reference Infrastructure Sharing Offer (RISO) approvals), improved security, rising customers, and early signs that revenue per user is getting healthier relative to costs.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Business Review — Kenya
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: 1. Financial Services/M-PESA
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: M-PESA delivered another strong performance, with revenue growing by 13.4% YoY to KShs 182.7Bn, driven by growth in both customer numbers and usage. The number of one-month active customers grew by 14.5% YoY to 40.99Mn. Transactional momentum remained robust, reflected by value growth of 8.9% to KShs 41.68Trn and volume growth of 251% to 46.41Bn, while chargeable transactions recorded even stronger expansion, with values up 17.0% and volumes increasing by 27.6%, reinforcing the resilience and depth of the M-PESA ecosystem. Chargeable transactions per active one-month customer rose by 11.5% YoY to 42.27.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The merchant base expanded by 71.0% to 3.1Mn, driven mainly by Pochi, which grew by 81.5% to 2.1Mn, while Lipa Na M-PESA merchants increased by 54.2% to 1.0Mn. Wealth managementalso gained traction, with AUM more than doubling to KShs 21.0Bn, driven by Ziidi’s strong uptake with AUM growing >100% to KShs 18.7Bn. During the year, we launched Ziidi Trader, enabling customers to seamlessly trade listed securities directly from their mobile phones. The platform expands M-PESA’s Wealth Management proposition beyond savings into active investing, supporting broader retail participation in capital markets. M-PESA now contributes 45.6% of total service revenue in Kenya from 44.2% in FY25.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: 2. Connectivity Business
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The Connectivity Business delivered steady growth, with revenue increasing 6.9% YoY to KShs 197.9Bn, accounting for 49.4% of
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: service revenue in Kenya, compared to 50.8% in the prior year. Mobile Data became the largest contributor to connectivity revenue, representing 42.1%, overtaking Voice at 41.3%, underscoring the continued shift in customer usage patterns. Messaging revenue declined by 11.8% YoY, driven by structural changes in customer behaviour as usage continues to migrate toward IP based and over the top messaging platforms, in line with global industry trends. Mobile incoming revenue grew by 15.5% YoY to KShs 9.1Bn, while content revenue increased marginally by 0.5% YoY to KShs 2.4Bn.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Mobile Data recorded strong performance, with revenue increasing 14.4% YoY to KShs 83.35Bn, supported by continued customer growth, increased usage and device penetration. One month active mobile data customers grew 11.2% YoY to 34.13Mn, while customers consuming more than 1GB per month increased 22.4% to 14.52Mn, signalling stronger engagement. Average data consumption per chargeable subscriber rose 16.6% YoY to 4.92GBs, while ARPU increased 2.6% YoY to KShs 274.00. We continue to enhance affordability through our targeted CVM initiatives. Rate per MB declining 12.1% YoY to 5.44 cents.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Growth was further underpinned by enhanced device penetration. The number of smartphones in our network grew 21.2% to 33.16Mn, expanding the addressable market for digital services. The migration toward higher capacity devices continued, with active 4G+ devices growing 31.8% to 30.78Mn, driven by 4G growth of 30.6% to 29.115Mn and 5G growth of 55.5% to 1.64Mn, supporting sustained growth in data consumption. Mobile Data now contributes 20.8% of total service revenue in Kenya, reinforcing its role as a core revenue growth pillar within the Connectivity portfolio.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Voice revenue grew 1.3% YoY to KShs 81.82Bn, supported by higher usage and a growth in customer base. Minutes of use (MOU) per subscriber increased 5.4% YoY to 211.61 minutes, while one month active voice customers grew 4.7% YoY to 31.55Mn, reflecting sustained engagement. This growth was partly offset by yield pressure, with the outgoing rate per minute declining 8.5% YoY to KShs 1.02, driven by targeted commercial offers focused on enhancing affordability and stimulating usage.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Messaging revenue declined 11.8% YoY to KShs 11.0Bn, as messages per subscriber fell 24.0% YoY to 121.45. The decline was partially mitigated by growth in the customer base, with one month active messaging customers increasing 24.7% YoY to 26.24Mn.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: 3. Fixed Service & loT
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Fixed Services and lol revenue grew 12.2% to KShs 20.20Bn, driven by increased connections and a strengthened value proposition. Growth was supported by a diversified portfolio across FTTH (Fiber to the Home), FTTB (Fiber to the Business), wholesale, and loT solutions. Fixed service and wholesale transit revenue rose by 11.7% YoY to KShs 19.07Bn, supported by strong growth in Consumer revenue, which increased by 19.5% YoY to KShs 9.03Bn, and a 5.5% YoY uplift in Enterprise fixed revenue to KShs 10.04Bn. loT revenue rose by 20.8% to KShs 1.13Bn.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Fixed connectivity continued to scale strongly, with FTTH customers increasing 35.0% YoY to 407.08k, driven by expanded fibre coverage and growing demand for high speed internet. Network expansion remained robust, with homes connected growing 45.9% YoY to 739.38k (532.97k six months active) and homes passed increasing 16.2% YoY to 807.02k. Enterprise fixed customers grew 19.7% YoY to 83.61k, reflecting sustained uptake among SMEs and corporates seeking reliable connectivity solutions. Overall connection growth was significantly supported by 5G Fixed Wireless Access (FWA), which contributed 52.3% of total connection growth, with FWA customers increasing 53.0% YoY to 132.06k, while fibre customers grew 25.8% YoY to 358.64k.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Earnings Before Interest Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) rose by 13.7% YoY to KShs 233.89Bn while Earnings Before Interest Tax (EBIT) grew by 15.3% YoY to KShs 182.30Bn during the period.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Net income increased by 24.7% YoY to KShs 119.10Bn, underpinned by strong contributions from M-PESA and Mobile Data. Performance was supported by continued expansion in the customer base, higher usage levels and effective monetisation.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Business Review — Ethiopia
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Service revenue recorded a strong growth of 58.3% YoY to KShs 14.08Bn, driven by customer growth across all revenue lines, as well as increased adoption and deeper market penetration. The revenue mix continued to evolve, with voice contribution rising to 21.4% of total service revenue, up from 15.1% in FY25, reflecting accelerating traction in voice services. Mobile Data remained the dominant revenue stream, accounting for 67.9% of total service revenue, compared to 75.4% in FY25, underscoring sustained demand while indicating a progressively more balanced revenue structure as the business scales.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Mobile incoming revenues contributed 5.1%, with the remaining 5.6% derived from Messaging, M-PESA and Fixed Services, supporting further diversification of revenue sources. Overall, Ethiopia contributed 12.5% to total Group service revenue growth, highlighting its growing strategic importance within the Group’s medium term growth portfolio. Customer momentum remained strong, with 90 day active customers surging 54.2% YoY to 13.63Mn, while one month active customers increased 48.3% YoY to 10.75Mnh, reflecting accelerating adoption and deepening engagement across the market.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Voice revenue surged by 123.9% YoY to KShs 3.01Bn, driven by sustained growth in the customer base and rising usage levels. One month active voice customers increased by 39.6% YoY to 8.50Mn, while 90 day active voice customers grew by 42.3% YoY to 11.13Mn, reflecting broad based adoption and deepening engagement. Usage trends remained positive, with outgoing minutes of use per subscriber increasing 13.6% YoY to 144.64, supported by improved monetisation, as ARPU increased 21.2% YoY to KShs 34.46.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Messaging revenue rose strongly by 82.3% YoY to KShs 169.38Mnhn, driven by growth in customers and higher usage intensity. One month active SMS customers grew 22.1% YoY to 3.64Mn, while 90 day active SMS customers increased 27.7% YoY to 6.17Mn, signalling expanding reach across the customer base. Usage also strengthened, with SMS usage per subscriber rising 38.4% YoY to 24.73.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Mobile Data revenue grew by 42.5% YoY to KShs 9.56Bn, driven by rapid customer acquisition and sustained increase in usage. One month active mobile data customer base expanded by 48.5% YoY to 7.84Mn, while 90 day active data customers increased by 46.3% YoY to 10.40Mnh, reflecting accelerating adoption and deepening customer engagement. Usage remained resilient, with average data consumption per subscriber rising 6.8% YoY to 6.90GB, supported by improved affordability and expanding network availability.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Overall, Mobile Data accounted for 67.9% of total service revenue in Ethiopia, reaffirming its position as the primary revenue driver while supporting the broader scaling of the business. Performance was supported by targeted Customer Value Management (CVM) initiatives, which enabled more personalised bundles and sustained customer engagement. These initiatives, alongside expanding network coverage and improved service quality, supported broader access, higher usage intensity and a more sustainable, diversified revenue base as the business continues to mature.

text: b) Measurement basis
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The measurement basis used is the historical cost basis except for investment property that has been measured at fair value.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Under the historical cost basis, assets are recorded at the amount of cash or cash equivalents paid or the fair value of the consideration given to acquire them at the time of their acquisition. Liabilities are recorded at the amount of proceeds received in exchange for the obligation or, in some cases, at the amounts of cash or cash equivalents expected to be paid to satisfy the liability in the normal course of business.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: c) Translation of foreign operations
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The results, cash flows and financial position of Group entities that have a functional currency different from the presentation currency of the Group are translated into the presentation currency as follows:
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Assets and liabilities, including goodwill and fair value adjustments arising on acquisition, are translated at rates of exchange ruling at the reporting date
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: . Specific transactions in equity are translated at rates of exchange ruling at the transaction dates
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: . Income and expenditure and cash flow items are translated at weighted average exchange rates for the period or translated at exchange rates at the date of the transaction, where applicable; and
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Foreign exchange translation differences are recognised in Other Comprehensive Income (OCI) and accumulated in the foreign currency translation reserve (FCTR), except to the extent the difference is allocated to non-controlling interests.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: An entity may have a monetary item that is receivable from a foreign operation. An item for which settlement is neither planned nor likely to occur in the foreseeable future is, in substance, a part of the entity’s net investment in that foreign operation. On consolidation, exchange differences arising from the translation of the net investment in foreign operations are taken to other comprehensive income and accumulated in the foreign currency translation reserve.

text: g. Ethiopia’s hyperinflationary status and exit from IAS 29
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Ethiopia was classified as a hyperinflationary economy in FY2022, when its three-year cumulative inflation exceeded 100%, meeting the threshold under IAS 29: Financial Reporting in Hyperinflationary Economies. The surge in inflation was driven by currency depreciation, fiscal imbalances, political instability, and global supply chain disruptions.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: As a result, IAS 29 was applied from December 2022, and Safaricom PLC restated its financial statements for the years ended 31 March 2023, 2024, and 2025 using the Consumer Price Index (CPI) - CP! measures the average change over time in prices paid by households for a standard basket of goods and services and is a key indicator of inflation. This impacted the presentation of income, assets, and equity, including recognition of net monetary gains.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Macroeconomic Stabilisation and Projected Exit
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: By May 2025, inflationary pressures had eased significantly. The IMF reported a three-year cumulative inflation rate of 109% as of December 2024 but projected a decline to 80% in 2025 and 54% in 2026. Ethiopia’s national statistics office reported a three-year rate of 92% and a 12-month rate of 14% as of May 2025. These trends, alongside improved currency stability and fiscal discipline, indicate Ethiopia will fall below IAS 29 thresholds by 30 June 2025.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The cumulative inflationary adjustments will unwind gradually through the financial statements over the coming years, in line with the remaining useful lives of the restated nonmonetary assets and liabilities. These adjustments will affect revenues, direct costs, and depreciation and amortisation.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: During the year, Safaricom Plc recognised a net impact of KES 76 billion across revenue, direct costs, and depreciation and amortisation, reflecting the unwinding of inflation-indexed balances previously recognised in respect of Ethiopia.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: M-PESA usage continues to grow as we accelerate new growth areas
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Velocity in the M-PESA ecosystem continued to accelerate in FY26, driven by sustained growth across our FinTech solutions including payments, lending, savings and international remittances. This reflects increasing customer engagement and higher frequency of transactions across both consumer and business use cases. During the year, the total value of M-PESA transactions grew 8.9% YoY to KShs 41.68Trn, while transaction volumes increased by a strong 25.1% YoY to 46.41Bn. The faster growth in volumes relative to value underscores rising usage intensity, supported by broader adoption and expanded use cases.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY26
author: Safaricom PLC

text: We continue to leverage our digital platforms, including the M-PESA Super App, to deliver an end to end, seamless customer experience across the ecosystem. The Super App brings together payments, savings, lending, wealth and global payments into a single, intuitive interface, enhancing convenience and driving deeper engagement. We now have 21.99Mn Consumer App sign ins, with 6.58Mn Active Consumers. On the enterprise side, adoption of the Business App continued to scale, with over 458.9k active business customers using the platform to accept payments, manage cash flows and access tailored financial solutions.

author: Safaricom PLC

text: A Transfers (P2P) All person-to-person funds transfer transactions to a registered /Unregistered M-PESA subscriber (Excludes transfers or payments to businesses). M-PESA Agents A business that has been onboarded to facilitate the transformation of cash to e-value via deposit and vice versa via withdrawal. An M-PESA agent may also be authorized to onboard new subscribers onto Safaricom or M-PESA as well as other sales and cross-sell activities at a commission. Withdrawals/ All financial transactions that involve a customer receiving cash from an M-PESA agent or ATM, withdrawn Cash out from their M-PESA wallet. All financial transactions that involve a customer giving cash to an M-PESA agent in exchange e-value into their M-PESA wallet. Deposits/ Cash in Payments C2B, B2C and C2B (Paybill) All person-to-business transactions which involve transfer of funds from a customer to a business B2B till (typically involving large business & excludes agent deposits or payments to medium or small businesses). B2C All business-to-person transactions which involve a transfer of funds from a business till to an individual customer (typically done by large business & excludes agent withdrawals). B2B All Business-to-Business transactions which involve transfer of funds from one business till to another business till (Excludes fund transfers within the same business to facilitate business operations). Lipa Na M-PESA All financial transactions that involve payments into or out of Lipa na M-PESA tills (Buy Goods & transacting (LNM) till). LNM has two major use cases; . Buy Goods - mainly used for one-off payments to merchants, this is done ‘on the go’, mainly face to face but can also be done remotely. Transacting Tills/Business Tills- The M-PESA Business till is an enhancement of the existing Lipa Na M-PESA Buy Goods till that enables business owners to collect payments on the till and use the money collected to make other transactions directly from their till. Pochi La Biashara __‘ Pochi La Biashara, translated to ‘Business Wallet’ in English, is a product that allows M-PESA registered customers who own informal businesses such as; food vendors, kiosk owners, boda-boda operators, second hand clothes dealers, etc. to receive and separate business funds from personal funds on their M-PESA line. Savings and Lending M-Shwari The M-Shwari is a micro-credit product which allows customers to borrow money or to complement their savings towards an investment or enterprise. The M-Shwari Deposit Account is a micro-savings product which allows customers to securely store their money for a specific purpose or for unexpected events. Safaricom provides support to NCBA (a tier 1 Kenyan Bank) in the roll-out of this product. KCB-M-PESA The KCB M-PESA is a micro-credit product which gives customers access to loans for an emergency or to fund a project or an enterprise. Safaricom provides support to KCB (a tier 1 Kenyan Bank) in the roll-out of this product.

author: Safaricom PLC

text: Fuliza Timiza Overdraft facility for businesses (Merchant OD) M-KOPA Taasi Pochi (Pochi Term Loan) Taasi Till (Merchant Term Loan) Ziidi MMF Ziidi Trader In partnership with Kenyan lenders, NCBA, KCB and Sidian Bank, Safaricom Kenya operates an Overdraft (OD) facility dubbed ‘Fuliza’, a product that enables customers to access unsecured line of credit by overdrawing on M-PESA to cover short-term cash-flow shortfalls subject to an applicable pre-determined limit. Fuliza is available to all M-PESA customers, however the awarding of limits will depend on the customer’s credit scoring and how long they have been using M-PESA. Customers who ‘opt in’ on Fuliza are charged a one-off access fee and daily maintenance fees on unpaid loan amounts based on a pre-determined matrix. In partnership with ABSA Kenya, Timiza is a wallet solution that offers easy banking and instant loans to customers. Through *848# or the Timiza app customers are able to get an instant loan, save, send money, pay bills, purchase airtime, and get insurance with Timiza. Merchant OD is a loan product in partnership with KCB Bank Kenya (KCB). The service enables business owners on Lipa Na M-PESA to complete payments even with insufficient funds in their till. The service applies when making transactions from a Lipa Na M-PESA Business Till to other Till Numbers and PayBill Numbers, when sending money to an individual, and when withdrawing to the nominated number or at an Agent. The service advances an overdraft of up to KShs 400,000 depending on the business’ limit. The overdraft is offered a 2% one off fee and a tiered daily access fee after the 24-hour free period. All financial transactions associated with the M-KOPA proposition, a buy-now-pay later product from the M-KOPA company e.g Devices, Solar. After an initial deposit, customers pay daily instalments via a mobile money service (M-PESA) until paying off the balance. Once this repayment is complete, customers own the unit outright. M-KOPA provides solar home systems and other that innovatively integrate machine-to-machine technology (M2M) with a micro-payment solution. The system includes embedded GSM technology for monitoring and metering usage, while its pay-as-you-go service carries the advantage of no large initial cash outlay. After an initial deposit, customers pay daily instalments via a mobile money service (M-PESA) until paying off the balance. Once this repayment is complete, customers own the unit outright. Importantly, this solution is cheaper and healthier than the alternative, kerosene lamps for rural households with no electricity. M-KOPA solar is currently available in 750 outlets nationwide in Kenya through the Safaricom distribution network. Taasi Pochi is a short-term credit facility in partnership with Sidian Bank and Pezesha Africa Limited, (Pezesha Africa Limited is a Kenyan fintech company that builds and provides digital lending infrastructure for small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs) in Sub-Saharan Africa) It provides instant loans ranging from KES 1,000 to KES 250,000 to businesses that operate through the Pochi La Biashara wallet. To qualify, a business must have at least six months of active transactions on the wallet. Taasi Till (Merchant Term Loan) is a financial product provided by Safaricom in partnership with Diamond Trust Bank (DTB) and Asante Finance, (Asante Financial Services Group, is a digital, credit-led neo-bank that provides financial services to Micro, Small, and Medium-sized Enterprises (MSMEs) and individuals in Sub- Saharan Africa) targeting businesses that use the Lipa Na M-PESA Buy Goods Till. It offers short-term loans ranging from KES 100 to KES 200,000, with repayment periods of 1, 7, or 21 days. Eligible businesses must have operated the till for at least three months and can only hold one loan per till at a time. Ziidi MMF is a mobile-based money market fund jointly offered by Safaricom (NSE: SCOM), Standard Investment Bank and ALA Capital Limited. The fund enables customers to invest directly from their M-PESA wallets, earning daily-accrued interest credited to their Ziidi wallet. Regulated by the Capital Markets Authority (CMA), Ziidi MMF offers transparent daily yields, simple onboarding via the M-PESA App or USSD (3345#), and no maximum investment limit, with the daily M-PESA transaction limit of KES 500,000 and a per-transaction limit of KES 250,000 applying. Ziidi Shariah complements the offering by expanding the ecosystem to provide inclusive, Shariah-compliant investment options — The current yield stands at 5.8% Ziidi Trader is a mobile-based share-trading platform jointly offered by Safaricom (NSE: SCOM), Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE) and Kestrel Capital (EA) Limited, a licensed investment bank and stockbroker in Kenya. Accessible through the M-PESA App, the platform enables customers to buy and sell NSE-listed shares and corporate bonds directly from their mobile phones, monitor portfolios, and access market insights

author: Safaricom PLC

text: Ziidi Trader Ziidi Trader is a mobile-based share-trading platform jointly offered by Safaricom (NSE: SCOM), Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE) and Kestrel Capital (EA) Limited, a licensed investment bank and stockbroker in Kenya. Accessible through the M-PESA App, the platform enables customers to buy and sell NSE-listed shares and corporate bonds directly from their mobile phones, monitor portfolios, and access market insights through a fully digital experience. Operating under the oversight of the Capital Markets Authority (CMA), Ziidi Trader ensures investor protection, transparency, and market integrity, while supporting informed long-term investing through clear disclosures and investor education. The platform allows customers to begin investing from as little as one share, providing a simple, secure, and fully digital access point to Kenya’s capital markets.

M-PESA Consumer App M-PESA Business App M-PESA Bill Manager Insurance The M-PESA App for consumers delivers the suite of M-PESA solutions to our consumers in a customer centric approach. It serves as a one stop shop for our customers with smartphone devices for various solutions. M-PESA for Business App allows merchants, agents and businesses to better visualize their collections and spend, see full statements and transact directly from their M-PESA Business till. The App provides users with a faster and simpler payment experience. Its an alternative to the USSD service *234# Option 2. This is a service that allows customers to invoice and reconcile payments against the invoices, memorizing all Paybills and account numbers and better still, a way for them to be reminded of the bill payment due dates. This is a solutions targeted to billers only. It can be accessed by dialling *234# then selecting M-PESA Products followed by Bill Manager. author: Safaricom PLC

text: Our focus for FY20 was to regain customer trust and market share. In line with this we launched the “For You” Customer proposition renewing our commitment to customers to be Simple, Transparent and Honest across all of our products and operations. This has led to improved customer sentiment, brand consideration and market share gain for the first time since 2017.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: We are keen on giving our customers flexibility and a more agile network. In FY20 we continued on our journey of digital transformation, automating across both our internal and customer facing operations and enhancing the use of artificial intelligence to inform products and processes. We ramped up our investment in IT capabilities, with an objective of mapping a monetization path in critical verticals such as agriculture, health, education and ecommerce.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: We completed the acquisition of the M-PESA brand, product development and support services from Vodafone Plc through a newly-created joint venture between ourselves and Vodacom. This initiative will enhance M-PESA’s growth in Africa by giving us both full control of the M-PESA brand, product development and support services as well as the opportunity to expand M-PESA into new African markets.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: We continue to be guided by the Sustainable Development Goals, which are not only influencing a more sustainable approach to business, but also strengthening our commitment to ensuring that we leave no-one behind. We continue to support the economy, from job creation to the taxes and duties we pay, and now source 74% of our procurement needs from local suppliers. We continue to support the communities we operate in, impacting millions of Kenyans each year and disbursing support on many projects from both our Safaricom and M-PESA foundations. And we do this while being environmentally conscious, we are targeting to become carbon neutral by 2050, and to support this have an ambitious target of planting 5 million trees in the next 5 years.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: We are very pleased about our performance for FY20, outperforming our EBIT guidance despite some top line challenge in the year. Service Revenue increased 4.8% driven by sustained customer acquisition, recovery of mobile data growth which is now back to double digit, along with sustained M-PESA and fixed data growth. The growth was partially offset by contraction of the betting industry and the free transaction fees associated with our Covid 19 response. On an underlying basis Service Revenue increased 5.9%.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: In line with global industry trends, voice and messaging revenue recorded a blended decline of 3.3%. This decline was partly driven by competitive pressures and migration to newer technologies, and partly by the impact of corrective actions taken last year to make it easier for our customers to manage their premium rate subscriptions, opt out of them and regain customer trust. Voice and messaging are now 44.4% of service revenue.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: M-PESA grew 12.6% YoY in the period. On an underlying basis, excluding the impact of betting and our COVID-19 response, M-PESA grew 17.2%. This growth was driven by savings and lending and P2P which make up two thirds of the total growth. However, we have seen a slowdown in the growth rates across withdrawals and payments, partly driven by a general economic slowdown, and this is likely to get worse as we face the coronavirus pandemic in FY21. While we are facing some short term headwinds, there is still a lot of opportunity to grow and we are excited about M-PESA’s future.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: We are pleased to report that on average our customers are now using more than 1GB per month and that mobile data achieved double digit revenue growth of 12.1% for the year. Mobile data now accounts for 16.2% of Service Revenue and grew 21.1% 2H20. Growth in mobile data was driven by increased smartphone penetration and usage and a 28.3% reduction in effective rate per MB. The launch of “For You” structure in October 2019 enhanced affordability and gave customers more control and worry-free experience when using mobile data.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: In the period, fixed service revenue registered a growth of 10.7% and contributes 3.6% of total service revenue in the period. Fixed revenue is driven by increased activity and penetration for FTTH.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: We sustained strong investment in FY20. Our capital additions amounted to KShs 36.10bn for the period. Capex intensity has reduced 1.1ppts YoY to 13.8% as we continue to focus on enhancing monetization and cost savings opportunities upon deployment.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The Board remains committed to investing in the business and continuing our strong record for paying progressive dividends each year. The proposed dividend for FY20 is KShs 56.09bn. The proposed dividend per share (DPS) of KShs 1.40 has been computed at 80% of the profit and total comprehensive income for the year excluding the one-off exceptional item of share of profit of joint venture of KShs 3.3bn, divided by number of issued share capital on IFRS 15/16 basis.

author: Safaricom PLC

text: Peter Ndegwa, Safaricom PLC CEO commented:
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: I have joined Safaricom at a time when humanity is facing its’ biggest challenge in modern history. The past one month of my time in Safaricom has been spent interacting with both staff and customers and I am pleased to say that I am filled with admiration for the resilience our staff are showing, by ensuring that in unprecedented times, our customers continue to interact with our products and services with ease.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Never has our purpose of transforming lives been more present and relevant. We continue to implement measures to cushion customers and Kenyans at large from the negative impact of the pandemic. Our current support which extends to 30 June 2020, is valued at KShs 6.5bn, this includes:

author: Safaricom PLC

text: • Safaricom has further supported the government in the establishment and operation of a 24-7 COVID-19 Information Centre, leveraging the capabilities of our Customer Contact Centre. We are also hosting over 300 doctors to support the frontline staff in educating, informing and managing the spread of COVID-19.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: • Customers are allowed to use Bonga points at any outlets with Lipa na M-PESA tills to buy food and basic necessities.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: • Over KShs 331mn set aside to help in education, health and empowerement to drive community support.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: It is important to point out that our most critical support to the country remains ensuring network stability to support the usage in M-PESA, voice, SMS and data. We have the responsibility to keep the country connected.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Safaricom has always been the pioneer in many ground-breaking innovations, and I am committed to continuing this path with a focus to tap into the vast opportunity in the Agriculture, Health, Education, and Public sectors. Leveraging the power or partnerships, and the digital platforms we operate, I aim to drive affordable and innovative products in mobile communication, financial services and enterprise solutions whilst maintaining leadership in the best network quality.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: I have a clear ambition to strengthen our differentiation and to lead the company in capturing the continued opportunities of digital.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Due to the uncertainty emanating from the COVID-19 pandemic, many parameters that would normally be factored in for a prudent guidance are unclear, and changing by the day. As a result, we have decided to postpone giving guidance until Q2 of FY21when we hope visibility on the situation improves. Whilst things will remain challenging in the short term, we believe we are well placed to weather this storm. We will leverage the strength of our balance sheet and our resilient business model to ensure we continue to innovate and generate efficiencies for our customers and shareholders alike thus safeguarding our performance for the future.

text: a. Basis of preparation
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The financial statements have been prepared on a going concern basis and in compliance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) issued by the International Accounting Standards Board. The financial statements are presented in Kenya Shillings (KShs), which is also the functional currency, rounded to the nearest billion (KShs bn), except where otherwise stated.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The preparation of the financial statements in conformity with IFRS requires the use of certain critical accounting estimates. It also requires the management to exercise its judgement in the process of applying the Group’s accounting policies. The areas involving a higher degree of judgement or complexity, or where assumptions and estimates are significant to the financial statements are disclosed in the detailed financial statements in Note 3.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The measurement basis used is the historical cost basis except where otherwise stated in the accounting policies summarised below.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: Under the historical cost basis, assets are recorded at the amount of cash or cash equivalents paid or the fair value of the consideration given to acquire them at the time of their acquisition. Liabilities are recorded at the amount of proceeds received in exchange for the obligation or, in some cases, at the amounts of cash or cash equivalents expected to be paid to satisfy the liability in the normal course of business.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: New and amended standards adopted by the Group
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The Group has applied the following standards and amendments for the first time for the annual reporting year commencing 1 April 2019:
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: i) Adoption of IFRS 16: Lease
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The Group has adopted IFRS 16 leases retrospectively from 1 April 2019 but has not restated comparatives for the year ended 31 March 2019, as permitted under the specific transition provisions in the standard. The reclassifications and the adjustments arising from the new leasing rules are therefore recognised in the opening balance sheet on1 April 2019.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: On adoption of IFRS 16, the group recognised lease liabilities in relation to leases which had previously been classified as ‘operating leases’ under the principles of IAS 17 Leases. These liabilities were measured at the present value of the remaining lease payments, discounted using the lessee’s incremental borrowing rate as of 1 April 2019.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The observable incremental borrowing rate applied to the lease liabilities on 1 April 2019 was 13.0% being the Central Bank of Kenya Rate (CBR) +400 basis points.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: ii) The Group’s leasing activities and significant accounting policies
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: The Group’s leases include base transceiver stations (BTS) sites, collocation sites, retail stores spaces, administrative office spaces and residential facilities. Lease terms are negotiated on an individual basis and contain a wide range of terms and conditions.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: After the adoption of IFRS 16, Leases are recognised as a right-of-use asset and a corresponding liability at the date at which the leased asset is available for use by the Group.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: b. Change in accounting estimate for useful life for specific Property Plant and Equipment asset categories.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: IAS 16.51 guides that the residual value and the useful life of an asset should be reviewed at least at each financial year-end and, if expectations differ from previous estimates, any change is accounted for prospectively as a change in estimate under IAS 8.
title: Safaricom Annual Report FY20
author: Safaricom PLC

text: On an annual basis, the Group through its internal technology team conducts an extensive review of the useful life of its Property Plant and Equipment assets. This year the Group reviewed and subsequently changed the accounting estimate on useful life for network assets. Subsequently the Group adopted a revised depreciation policy effective 1 April 2019. In the period, underlying depreciation charge on the asset categories reduced by KShs 2.30bn.

text: In the year, Safaricom and Vodacom completed the acquisition of the M-PESA brand, product development and support services from Vodafone through a newly-created joint venture, with 50-50 share ownership. This initiative will enhance M-PESA’s growth in Africa by giving both Vodacom and Safaricom full control of the M-PESA brand, product development and support services as well as the opportunity to expand M-PESA into new African markets.
